issue.title: Port the failure-aware session and clan rollup to sase-core
issue.description: Listed as an out-of-scope follow-up in epic sase-1ux's plan (plan:202611/failed_clan_visibility.md, "Porting the session/clan rollup itself to sase-core"); filed by the sase-1ux land agent. Today the session-root rollup (apply_status_overrides session branch in src/sase/ace/tui/models/_agent_status_apply.py: failure frontier, not-adopted exclusion), the clan roster / tribe summary readers, and FailureFocus (src/sase/ace/tui/models/failure_focus.py) are TUI-only Python. The CLI, gateway, web, and Telegram frontends therefore cannot report the same FAILED / NOT ADOPTED session state the Agents tab now shows. The epic left FailureFocus and tests/ace/tui/models/test_failure_rollup_consistency.py as the seam for a later port.

task_type_fields.proposal: Move the session-root status/bucket rollup (failure frontier, not-adopted handoff exclusion, superseded-failure handling) and the FailureFocus projection into sase_core with a Python binding, make the TUI consume it, and keep test_failure_rollup_consistency.py as the cross-surface contract.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-1ux's goal was making the Agents tab truthful; its plan explicitly deferred the core port so the TUI fix could land first, keeping FailureFocus as the seam.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1ux built one failure-aware session rollup plus FailureFocus in Python and explicitly left the sase-core port out of scope; the Rust core boundary rule says behavior other frontends must match belongs in sase-core.
